competences: The learner recognises the three colours on a traffic-light chart.
The learner matches red, orange and green to stop, get ready and go.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, reads, spells and writes: traffic, lights, red, orange, green, stop.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to name the three traffic-light colours.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to match each colour to the meaning taught in the school source.
priorKnowledge: The previous lesson introduced traffic lights as one of the signs guiding road users; this lesson names their colours and the school-source meanings.
materials: Traffic-light chart with red, orange and green clearly labelled
Word cards for stop, get ready and go
references: P I Literacy Scheme OF Work Term III
P I Literacy Lesson Notes Term III

steps.content: Transport pictures and the starter question: Name the three colours of the traffic lights.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher displays traffic-light chart with red, orange and green clearly labelled and asks: "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." Learners first identify familiar pictures; the teacher connects their responses to traffic lights.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners look at the transport pictures, identify familiar words, and give oral responses to the starter question before copying any notes.

steps.stage: Development: Three colours of the traffic lights
steps.content: Three colours of the traffic lights: Red Orange Green
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Red Orange Green Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for three colours of the traffic lights, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning of the traffic lights
steps.content: Meaning of the traffic lights: Red means stop. Orange means get ready. Green means go.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher points to the relevant transport pictures and writes these points on the board: Red means stop. Orange means get ready. Green means go. Using guided discussion, the teacher asks: "Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green." and checks that learners identify the corresponding pictures or words.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the pictures and words for meaning of the traffic lights, answer the quoted question, and copy the short points into their books.

steps.content: 1. Name the three colours of the traffic lights. 2. Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green. 3. Draw and shade the traffic lights.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the sourced exercise: "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." "Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green." "Draw and shade the traffic lights." The teacher reads each item clearly, checks individual answers, and uses the transport chart to correct mistaken identifications.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the exercise questions in their books, complete any specified matching or drawing, and correct their responses with the teacher.

source.quote: Name the three colours of the traffic lights

steps.content: Key points: Red Orange Green; Red means stop. Orange means get ready. Green means go.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher checks the lesson objectives using these exercise items: "Name the three colours of the traffic lights." "Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green." "Draw and shade the traffic lights." The teacher confirms correct answers against the board notes and identifies learners needing further picture-supported practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners give short oral answers, compare them with the transport pictures and board notes, and correct any remaining errors in their books.

assessment: Check the written exercise and oral responses: Name the three colours of the traffic lights. Write the meaning of the traffic lights: red, orange and green. Draw and shade the traffic lights. Mark against the source-based answers and revisit incorrect identifications using the transport chart.
homework: Complete or correct this sourced exercise item in your book: Draw and shade the traffic lights.
